doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Ernest on second lining
summary: Ernest followed bands as a boy; they discuss banjo and bass in parades.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Better get back to, uh, Ernest. Now, let's see. You were talking about some of the outstanding bands. Did you have a second line much?
Oh, yeah. A lot of times. I loved that.
How old were you when you started second line?
I was about 14, 15 years old. Something like that. Mm-hmm. Yeah.
Would you sneak away from school a little?
Oh, a lot of times. I was going to play a little Rikki Nine until he called up with me.
Well, what bands did you follow?
Oh, in fact, anyone I'd see. I was ready to go.
Do you remember the names of any of them?

Well, I remember Emanuel Perez and them. I don't remember the name of the band, but I mean, some of the players, you know, you should be in the band, old times. Buddy Madden and all of them, them days. Joe Oliver. Did you like any one of them the best? Anywhere music was, I just had liked music, you know? That's what I said. I started there. I didn't finish, though. I regret it that many did.
Did many piano players play parades? Let's see now. Santiago plays snare drum. I never thought about that too much. You know Lester, Blackie? He plays snare drum. I've seen him in the streets.
I think I do know him. Yeah.

I'm trying to think about any of the others that they ever play parades, like Deku. That's something we ought to follow up on. Some of the banjo players, some of them even took their banjo on the street. Oh, yeah. I've seen that.

Danny Buff and Joyce Gaino both did that. Both of them. And Doc Ernest took his bass one day. Right? I love to see that. I like to see that, too. I will, too. He must have tied it on him. They do that in Philadelphia.
They have bands that have bass fiddles. It's a mama.
Yeah. Put on a little dog. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Big. I don't know what they do. Put on a little wagon and somebody pull it. That's what it's like. I hope so. They sure will get tied.

They have something about automobiles. They're some piano players trying to carry the piano. Yeah. Some of them will try. Oh, yeah. Of course, they make them smaller now. Oh, yeah. Yeah, that time. I have a piano. Yeah, piano, them days.
